lines: A friend of ours was taken in high school. For a whole year, nobody knew where she was.
Today, people are sold through social media ads, shot in rooms that look like any other apartment. Investigators get the photos. They almost never get the address.
So we built Dome. A dome over the search area, that shrinks to one building.
Five AI agents, under one LangChain deep agents supervisor, turn flagged accounts into a ranked list of buildings.

First, the Linker. Accounts that share sticky notes, the same phone, the same wallet, the same photos, the same reworded script, get joined into one ring. One shared clue is only a hint. It takes two different kinds to make a link.
The Zoner reads place clues, like landmarks and area codes, and draws the dome. An area, never a pin.
The Lister pulls every CoStar building inside the dome, and keeps the ones that fit the photos.
The Locator matches the ad photos to rooms inside Matterport 3D scans, then checks the window view against Vexcel aerial imagery. That also fixes the scan's location.
And the Briefer ranks every building, high, medium or low, with a score and plain reasons.
On our test case, twelve accounts became one ring. Ten square kilometers became seven buildings. And one building came back High, with a score of sixty six.
Every result is a lead for a human to verify. Dome can't contact or dispatch anyone, and every decision it makes is logged.
Synthetic accounts. Real building data. Dome helps task force analysts find the room, so they can find the person, faster.
